title: Publish a normative consumer verification procedure

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as the normative ten-layer verification procedure and executable conformance fixtures.

provenance.source_label: Kimi K3 extension: consumer verification story
provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Add one paragraph explaining how a receiver recomputes every hash. The format carries receipts; teach receivers to check them, and lossless becomes a claim rather than a hope.
feedback.normalized_claim: Provide an executable, normative sequence for parsing, reconstructing, hashing, resolving aliases, and rejecting malformed or incomplete packets.

current_behavior: The in-band guide explains addresses, trust, terminators, aliases, omissions, and optional tasks but not digest preimages or a complete verification algorithm.
The repository parser verifies exact chunk framing and reconstructed content hashes for non-alias exact files.
Manifest JSON is emitted as a sidecar and manifest_sha256 is exposed, but a consumer-facing procedure for recomputing it is not normative.
The supplied explainer draft describes verification more strongly than the current parser and digest semantics support and therefore requires correction before adoption.

proposal.summary: Publish verification levels and reference test vectors so consumers can distinguish structural parsing, exact-file verification, manifest verification, completeness verification, and optional authenticity verification.
candidate_changes: Define ordered verification steps and mandatory rejection conditions for strict consumers.
Provide canonical digest preimages and small valid, tampered, truncated, nested, aliased, and encoded test vectors.
Document how aliases inherit canonical bytes and symbols without accidentally hashing alias metadata as file content.
Ship or expose a verification command whose output reports each checked claim and unavailable verification layer.
non_goals: Do not claim a parser verified packet fields it did not inspect.
Do not equate integrity, completeness, authenticity, semantic correctness, and repository completeness.
Do not make prose the only conformance artifact when executable test vectors are feasible.

questions: Which checks are mandatory for conformance and which are optional verification levels?
Should verification reconstruct every file eagerly or support verified selective access?
How should consumers report packets that are structurally readable but unverifiable at one layer?
risks: Documentation can drift from the generator without shared executable vectors.
A single pass or fail result can obscure which claims were actually verified.
Eager verification of very large packets can increase startup cost.
evidence_needed: Normative valid and invalid packet corpus with expected verification outcomes.
At least one independent parser or verifier run against the same vectors.
Measured verification cost for large packets and selective-access designs.
